beats.narration: The final module, wrapped. Five takeaways. Same test, one last time: if you can teach each one to a teammate, it's yours.

One: package while the build is fresh — parameters, docs, eval, and audit log travel together, because reconstruction is the expensive path. Two: a maintainer accepts what they can verify — focused code, a runnable example, a test, named assumptions, and the rights cleared first. Three: pin what ships — the platform follows the customer's cloud, the pinned ID makes an upstream change deliberate, and the prior version stays as the rollback. Four: measure the dimension that decides the placement — latency from the customer's region, compliance as pass-or-fail, cost as the total per call. Five: mark every seam as a boundary — the app is only as contained as its most privileged seam, and trust never carries over.

2. maintainers accept what they can VERIFY
3. pin what ships — prior version = the rollback
4. measure what decides — region · pass/fail · total cost
5. every seam = a boundary — trust never carries over

beats.narration: And that completes the arc — and the course. From tokens and context windows, through production prompting and agents, Claude Code and MCP, evals and security, to assets a regulated customer can audit and a team can reuse. Five modules, one developer track. Congratulations — you made it to the end.
